digest.top_line: DBCG Skagen 1: 40Gy/15fx locoregional RT noninferior to 50Gy/25fx for 3yr lymphedema (8.0% vs 9.4%, OR 0.84), N=2,908.
digest.tldr: Hypofractionation crosses into the nodal volumes START-B and FAST-Forward largely left untested: 15fx locoregional RT holds arm lymphedema at 3yr with no locoregional recurrence signal (HR 0.96). Breast carried the day. Caveat is maturity, not design: 1° EP is a 3yr morbidity endpoint, and BC mortality HR 1.25 (0.93-1.66) sits on 5.25yr median f/u.

sites.intro: Nodal-volume hypofractionation tested on a morbidity endpoint, with oncologic outcomes still immature.

studies.name: DBCG Skagen Trial 1
studies.tldr: 40Gy/15fx locoregional RT noninferior for 3yr lymphedema, 8.0% vs 9.4%, OR 0.84, with no recurrence or mortality differences.
details: 🔍 Phase III noninferiority, N=2,908 ITT (1,444 → 50Gy/25fx, 1,464 → 40Gy/15fx), 17 Danish centers, 2015-2021
📊 1° EP arm lymphedema at 3yr: 9.4% (50Gy) vs 8.0% (40Gy), OR 0.84 (95% CI 0.62-1.14), P = .27
📐 Noninferiority margin was max 5-percentage-point excess with 40Gy, assuming 10% 3yr incidence on 50Gy; met
🔍 High-risk BC with an indication for locoregional RT, median age 57 (range 23-86)
🔍 Accrual continued until 3yr lymphedema estimates were available in 1,012 pts
🔗 Extends START-B / UK FAST-Forward hypofractionation to the nodal volumes those trials largely did not test
⚠️ 1° EP was 3yr lymphedema, not a late-morbidity or cancer endpoint; fibrosis, brachial plexopathy and cardiac dose effects mature later
⚠️ BC mortality HR 1.25 (0.93-1.66) is null but the CI does not exclude a 66% relative excess; underpowered for oncologic outcomes
⚠️ Median f/u 4.1yr for lymphedema and 5.25yr for cancer outcomes is short for locoregional recurrence in a high-risk node-positive cohort

verdict.rationale: Adequately powered phase III noninferiority, prespecified primary endpoint met, 2,908 pts, with concordant recurrence and mortality signals. Directly licenses nodal hypofractionation.
verdict.audience: High-risk breast cancer with an indication for locoregional (nodal) radiotherapy

studies.significance: The unresolved question was never breast-only hypofractionation, it was the nodal volume: 40Gy/15fx delivered locoregionally produced no excess arm lymphedema at 3yr (8.0% vs 9.4%, OR 0.84) with locoregional recurrence HR 0.96. That moves 15-fraction treatment from breast/chest wall to the full locoregional target.
studies.monday_clinic: In high-risk breast cancer needing nodal irradiation, this supports 40Gy/15fx over 50Gy/25fx on lymphedema and locoregional control grounds; it does not speak to late fibrosis, plexopathy, or cardiac endpoints beyond 5 years of follow-up.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Phase III **noninferiority** RCT, 17 centers, accrual 2015-2021. 2,963 consented, **ITT 2,908** (1,444 at 50Gy, 1,464 at 40Gy). Accrual continued until 3-year lymphedema estimates were reported in 1,012 patients.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **High-risk breast cancer with an indication for locoregional radiotherapy**, the node-positive population where DBCG standard had been 50Gy/25fx. Median age **57** (range 23-86).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Standard arm **50Gy/25fx**, experimental arm **40Gy/15fx**, both delivered to the **locoregional** target rather than breast or chest wall alone. This is the volume where hypofractionation has been adopted least, on morbidity grounds.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: arm lymphedema at 3 years.** Noninferiority predefined as a maximum **5-percentage-point excess** with 40Gy against an assumed 10% incidence on 50Gy. Cancer outcomes (locoregional recurrence, distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality, all-cause mortality) were assessed within 8 years.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary endpoint met: 3-year lymphedema **9.4% vs 8.0%**, OR 0.84 (0.62-1.14), P = .27. Cancer outcome hazard ratios are in the detail table and showed **no differences by random assignment**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: START-B established 40Gy/15fx and FAST-Forward pushed to 26Gy/5fx, but both were dominated by breast or chest wall targets, leaving the nodal volume unsettled and 50Gy/25fx entrenched for locoregional treatment. Skagen 1 tests exactly that gap, and the direction matches the earlier trials rather than departing from them.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents high-risk breast cancer receiving locoregional radiotherapy on a DBCG-style 15-fraction schedule. Does not represent ultrahypofractionated 5-fraction nodal treatment, nor patients whose relevant morbidity endpoint is late fibrosis or plexopathy beyond this follow-up.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Lymphedema at 3 years is an early read on a toxicity that accrues for a decade, and the trial is not powered for the oncologic endpoints it reports: the breast cancer mortality HR of **1.25 (0.93-1.66)** is null but its upper bound is compatible with a real excess. Follow-up of **5.25 years** is short relative to the 8-year window the recurrence analyses describe.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The result settles the morbidity objection that kept 25 fractions alive for nodal targets, and does so on the endpoint the objection was actually about. What it does not settle is whether the mortality point estimates drift with maturity, or whether the same license extends below 15 fractions.

studies.interpretation:
Hypofractionation for breast cancer has been settled for the breast and chest wall for over a decade, and unsettled for the nodes for the same decade, for one reason: the objection was never about tumor control. START-B and its successors made 15 fractions routine where the target was the breast; the reluctance to carry that schedule into the supraclavicular fossa and axilla rested on a morbidity argument, specifically that a larger dose per fraction delivered across lymphatics already disturbed by surgery would drive arm swelling. Skagen 1 is designed to answer that objection directly rather than obliquely: it randomizes the fractionation and takes arm lymphedema as its primary endpoint, which is the correct architecture for the question actually in dispute.

On that question the answer is clean. The 3-year lymphedema rate was 8.0% with 40Gy/15fx against 9.4% with 50Gy/25fx, odds ratio 0.84 (0.62 to 1.14), comfortably inside a margin that would have tolerated a 5-percentage-point excess. Two features of that result deserve more weight than the p-value. First, the point estimate favors the hypofractionated arm rather than merely failing to exclude it, so the reader is not being asked to accept a small real harm hiding under a generous margin. Second, the observed rate on the standard arm came in close to the 10% the trial assumed, meaning the margin was calibrated against a realistic event rate rather than inflated by an overestimate of baseline risk, which is the usual way a noninferiority margin quietly becomes too easy to clear.

The oncologic endpoints should be read as reassurance rather than as evidence. Locoregional recurrence at a hazard ratio of 0.96 (0.62 to 1.51) is the most relevant of them for a radiation oncologist, and it is consistent with the biology one would predict from the isoeffective dose calculation, but the confidence interval spans a range wide enough that this trial could not have detected a modest real difference. The breast cancer mortality hazard ratio of 1.25 (0.93 to 1.66) is the number a skeptic will raise, and the honest response is not that it is non-significant but that the trial was never sized to adjudicate it; the same interval width that makes the locoregional result unpersuasive as proof of equivalence makes the mortality result unpersuasive as a signal of harm. With a median follow-up of 5.25 years reporting outcomes described within an 8-year window, the mortality estimates in particular are built on limited events and will move.

What should genuinely temper enthusiasm is the timescale of the primary endpoint relative to the toxicity it measures. Lymphedema accrues over many years, and a 3-year read captures the early and largely surgical component better than the late radiation-attributable one. The same caution applies with more force to the toxicities the trial does not report here: subcutaneous fibrosis, shoulder morbidity, brachial plexopathy, and cardiac effects all have latencies that make a 4- to 5-year follow-up uninformative. The trial's design does not preclude those from being answered later; it simply has not answered them yet.

The practical consequence is narrower than "hypofractionate everything" and larger than a marginal convenience gain. For a patient with an indication for nodal irradiation, the specific reason to spend 25 fractions rather than 15 has now been tested on its own terms and did not hold up. That does not license 5-fraction nodal treatment, which is a different dose per fraction against the same vulnerable structures and needs its own trial.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The gap this closes is volume, not schedule: 40Gy/15fx to the full locoregional target gave 3yr lymphedema of 8.0% vs 9.4% (OR 0.84) with locoregional recurrence HR 0.96 (0.62-1.51). The morbidity objection that kept 25 fractions alive for nodal treatment does not survive its own endpoint.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Shortening locoregional RT from 5 weeks to 3 without added arm morbidity compresses the adjuvant timeline, relevant when sequencing RT against adjuvant systemic therapy or capecitabine and olaparib in residual disease. No difference in distant recurrence (HR 1.10) or all-cause mortality (HR 1.08).

papers.title: Hypo- Versus Standard Fractionated Locoregional Radiotherapy of Patients With High-Risk Breast Cancer in the Randomized Phase III Trial: The Danish Breast Cancer Group Skagen Trial 1
authors: on behalf of the DBCG RT Committee
papers.abstract: PURPOSE Adjuvant radiotherapy for node-positive breast cancer (BC) using 50Gy/25fx has been Danish Breast Cancer Group (DBCG) standard. Hypofractionated radiotherapy based on 40Gy/15fx has been increasingly used; however, it is less frequently for locoregional therapy because of concern over more morbidity. DBCG Skagen trial 1 hypothesized that 40Gy/15fx did not cause more lymphedema than 50Gy/25fx 3 years after radiotherapy without compromising the pattern of failure. METHODS Skagen trial 1 is a phase III, noninferiority trial randomly assigning high-risk BC patients with an indication for locoregional radiotherapy to standard 50Gy/25fx versus experimental 40Gy/15fx. The primary end point was arm lymphedema; assuming a 3-year incidence with 50Gy/25fx of 10%, noninferiority was predefined to maximum 5% excess incidence with 40Gy/15fx. Accrual continued until 3-year estimates were reported in 1,012 patients. RESULTS Between 2015 and 2021, 2,963 patients consented from 17 centers; the intention-to-treat cohort comprised 2,908 patients: 1,444 had 50Gy (50%), and 1,464 had 40Gy (50%). The median age was 57 years (range, 23-86). At a median follow-up of 4.1 years (IQR, 3.0-5.0), the 3-year rates of lymphedema were 9.4% (50Gy) versus 8.0% (40Gy), odds ratio 0.84 (95% CI, 0.62 to 1.14), and P = .27, thus within the +5-percentage-point noninferiority margin. The median follow-up for cancer outcomes was 5.25 years (IQR, 4.26 to 6.96). Within 8 years, the hazard ratio for locoregional recurrence was 0.96 (95% CI, 0.62 to 1.51), that for distant recurrence was 1.10 (95% CI, 0.89 to 1.37), that for BC mortality was 1.25 (95% CI, 0.93 to 1.66), and that for all-cause mortality was 1.08 (95% CI, 0.85 to 1.36), thus all with no differences by random assignment. CONCLUSION 40Gy/15fx for locoregional radiotherapy of BC did not result in more lymphedema compared with 50Gy/25fx. There were no differences in locoregional or distant recurrences, breast cancer mortality, nor all-cause mortality between the random assignment arms.
